title: Help shape the future of food safety: Join an FSA Scientific Advisory Committee
authors: Professor Ian Young CBE, Chief Scientific Adviser

content.content: Cymraeg

In my role as Chief Scientific Adviser at the Food Standards Agency (FSA), I would like to invite you to help shape the future of food safety by joining one of the FSA's Scientific Advisory Committees.

At the FSA we are committed to ensuring that food is safe, authentic, healthier and more sustainable. Science sits at the heart of everything we do, helping us make evidence-based decisions that protect consumers and support a trusted food system.
This is why I am delighted to encourage you to apply for membership of one of our Scientific Advisory Committees, including the Science Council.
What is the role of the FSA’s Scientific Advisory Committees?
Our committees provide independent scientific advice on a wide range of issues, from food and feed safety to microbiological risks, toxicity of chemicals, novel foods, and emerging technologies.
Their expertise helps ensure that FSA policies and decisions are informed by the best available evidence and reflect the latest scientific developments.
Who are we looking for?

We are seeking individuals with a broad range of scientific knowledge, skills, and experience including pathology, neurotoxicity, microbiology, proteomic and metabolomic analysis, animal feed safety, chemical contaminants in food, social science and more.

Whether you are at the beginning of your career, an established expert in your field, or have specialist expertise that can bring a fresh perspective to our discussions, we encourage you to consider applying.
We are particularly keen to attract applicants from diverse professional backgrounds, sectors, and communities to ensure our committees benefit from a wide range of viewpoints and experiences.
Why should you consider applying?
Serving on an FSA Scientific Advisory Committee is a unique opportunity to contribute to issues of national importance, work alongside leading experts, and help shape the future of UK food policies.
It is also a rewarding way to apply your expertise in the public interest and make a tangible difference to consumers.
Additionally, if you’re a university employee, this role can contribute to your next Research Excellence Framework (REF) return.
When/how can you apply?
We are actively recruiting throughout September and until 12 October 2026.
Details of the vacancies and more information on how you can apply can be found on GOV.UK.

Please also help us spread the word by sharing these vacancies with colleagues and professional networks. Together, we can continue to ensure that the UK's food system is underpinned by world-class scientific advice.

Yn rhinwedd fy swydd fel Prif Gynghorydd Gwyddonol yr Asiantaeth Safonau Bwyd (ASB), hoffwn eich gwahodd i helpu i lunio dyfodol diogelwch bwyd drwy ymuno ag un o Bwyllgorau Cynghori Gwyddonol yr ASB.

Yn yr ASB rydyn ni wedi ymrwymo i sicrhau bod bwyd yn ddiogel, yn ddilys, yn iachach ac yn fwy cynaliadwy. Mae gwyddoniaeth wrth wraidd popeth a wnawn, gan ein helpu i wneud penderfyniadau ar sail tystiolaeth er mwyn diogelu defnyddwyr a chefnogi system fwyd y gellir ymddiried ynddi.
Dyna pam rwy’n falch iawn o’ch annog i wneud cais i fod yn aelod o un o’n Pwyllgorau Cynghori Gwyddonol, gan gynnwys y Cyngor Gwyddoniaeth.
Beth yw rôl Pwyllgorau Cynghori Gwyddonol yr ASB?

Mae ein pwyllgorau yn darparu cyngor gwyddonol annibynnol ar ystod eang o faterion, o ddiogelwch bwyd a bwyd anifeiliaid i risgiau microbiolegol, gwenwyndra cemegion, bwydydd newydd, a thechnolegau sy’n dod i’r amlwg.
Mae eu harbenigedd yn helpu i sicrhau bod polisïau a phenderfyniadau’r ASB yn cael eu llywio gan y dystiolaeth orau sydd ar gael ac yn adlewyrchu’r datblygiadau gwyddonol diweddaraf.
Am bwy rydyn ni’n chwilio?

Rydyn ni’n chwilio am unigolion sydd ag ystod eang o wybodaeth, sgiliau a phrofiad gwyddonol, gan gynnwys ym meysydd patholeg, niwrowenwyndra, microbioleg, dadansoddi proteomig a metabolomig, diogelwch bwyd anifeiliaid, halogion cemegol mewn bwyd, gwyddor gymdeithasol a mwy.

P’un a ydych chi ar ddechrau’ch gyrfa, yn arbenigwr sefydledig yn eich maes, neu fod gennych chi arbenigedd a all ddod â safbwynt newydd i’n trafodaethau, rydyn ni’n eich annog i ystyried gwneud cais.
Rydyn ni’n arbennig o awyddus i ddenu ymgeiswyr o gymunedau, sectorau a chefndiroedd proffesiynol amrywiol, er mwyn sicrhau bod ein pwyllgorau’n elwa o ystod eang o safbwyntiau a phrofiadau.
Pam dylech chi ystyried gwneud cais?

Mae gwasanaethu ar un o Bwyllgorau Cynghori Gwyddonol yr ASB yn gyfle unigryw i gyfrannu at faterion sydd o bwys cenedlaethol, i weithio ochr yn ochr ag arbenigwyr blaenllaw, ac i helpu i lunio dyfodol polisïau bwyd y DU.
Mae hefyd yn ffordd werth chweil o roi’ch arbenigedd ar waith er budd y cyhoedd ac o wneud gwahaniaeth gwirioneddol i ddefnyddwyr.
Yn ogystal, os ydych chi’n gweithio mewn prifysgol, gall y rôl hon gyfrannu at eich ffurflen nesaf ar gyfer y Fframwaith Rhagoriaeth Ymchwil (REF).
Pryd/Sut gallwch chi wneud cais?
Byddwn ni wrthi’n recriwtio drwy gydol mis Medi hyd nes 12 Hydref 2026.
Mae manylion y swyddi gwag a mwy o wybodaeth am sut gallwch chi wneud cais ar gael ar GOV.UK.

Hefyd, a fyddech cystal â’n helpu ni i ledaenu’r gair drwy rannu’r swyddi gwag hyn gyda chydweithwyr a rhwydweithiau proffesiynol? Gyda’n gilydd, gallwn ni barhau i sicrhau bod system fwyd y DU yn cael ei hategu gan gyngor gwyddonol o’r radd flaenaf.

title: Back to school with IP

content.content: School’s starting soon, it’s a big part of your every year beginning. Whether you're heading to secondary school, college or university, it's a time for new experiences, new trends and, of course, new school supplies.

We're Arwen and Freya, and we're spending our work experience with the Intellectual Property Office (IPO) social media team. Today, we're taking over the IPO Blog to share what we've learned about intellectual property (IP) and uncover the protection behind the everyday items we use at school. What do pens, pencils, notebooks and backpacks have in common? They can all be protected by IP.
Get ready for school with us

One of the first things we make sure we get right for the new school year is our shoes. We need something comfortable enough to wear all day, whether we're in lessons, walking between classes or spending time with friends.

This year we both chose to go with Nike trainers. Nike uses trade marks to protect its brand, including protecting their name and iconic 'Swoosh' logo. Nike trade marks help customers recognise Nike products and identify the business they come from.
Next up is bags
Although we're both getting ready for the new school year, our choices for bags are very different. Freya's going for a Coach bag, while Arwen's go-to bag is a Vans backpack.

Coach is a well known luxury brand. While the sizes can be big or small, totes are the way to go during these times. It’s big and practical – perfect for carrying all of your back to school equipment. Coach has protected its logo and name with a trademark. Check out some of their trade marks: Coach’s Trade marks

Vans has built a strong and recognisable brand, protecting its identity through a portfolio of trade marks including its famous logo. These trade marks help customers identify genuine Vans products and distinguish them from other brands.

Trade marks can protect names, logos and slogans. They help businesses protect their brands and help customers recognise where products and services come from. Find out more about trade marks and how to apply: Register a trade mark : Overview - GOV.UK
Inside our pencil case

One of the most important things for life in education is your stationery. Our go-to stationery is Staedtler. The brand is known for its Norris pencils which are famously known as the black and yellow ones that many people across the UK will recognise from their classrooms and pencil cases.
The Noris name is protected by a trade mark, helping Staedtler protect its brand and making it easier for customers to identify genuine products.

Staedtler has also used registered designs to protect the appearance of some of its products. Design protection can cover the look of an item, helping businesses safeguard features that make their products distinctive.
The smart board that powers our lessons

One piece of technology that has become a common sight in classrooms is the smart board. These interactive displays allow teachers and students to write, draw and interact with digital content directly on the screen, helping to make lessons more engaging.
Technology like this is often protected by patents. A patent protects new inventions and gives the owner the right to stop others from making, using or selling the invention without permission

Our work experience at the IPO has shown us that intellectual property is everywhere — even in the classroom. Trade marks, designs and patents all play a part in protecting the products we rely on, helping businesses stay innovative and helping consumers trust what they buy. As we head into the new school year, we will think about the items in our bags that have more behind them than meets the eye.

description: School's starting soon! Work experience students Arwen and Freya are taking over the IPO blog to explore the intellectual property behind their back-to-school essentials.

title: One week left to apply for roles on UK National Screening Committee

content.content: There is just one week left for people to apply for one of 4 vacancies on the UK National Screening Committee (UK NSC).
The UK NSC is looking to appoint 4 new expert members to support its work advising ministers and the NHS in the 4 UK countries about all aspects of screening.
The independent scientific committee is looking for individuals with a track record of national achievements in one of the following 4 roles:
How to apply
To find out more, including how to apply, please see the role descriptions and candidate information pack.
The closing date for applications is midday on Tuesday 8 September 2026.
Completed applications should be emailed to appointments.team@dhsc.gov.uk.
For any enquiries, please email  uknsc@dhsc.gov.uk
UK NSC and its host organisation the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) value and promote diversity. We encourage applications from all sections of the community.
About the roles

As well as specialist skills in their own particular area, candidates should be able to understand and critically consider complex information and scientific and/or medical data and have excellent communication skills.
Lay members should have the desire to make an effective contribution as a representative of all patients, carers and members of the public. See additional information about the role of PPV members.
Post holders are not paid but do receive travel and other related expenses.
Appointment term: successful candidates are usually appointed for a 3-year term, up to a maximum of 3 terms (totalling 9 years).

Commitment: The UK NSC meets 3 times a year to discuss and agree screening recommendations. Members are also required to engage in the development of documents relating to committee business throughout their term.
Keep up to date

The UK NSC blog provides up to date news from the UK NSC. You can register to receive updates direct to your inbox, so there is no need to keep checking for new articles. If you have any questions about this blog article, or about the work of the UK NSC, please email uknsc@dhsc.gov.uk.
